kg_child_context_reason: Generated fragments instantiate sd_crc_16 four times and depend on exact child port names, directions, reset/clock behavior, and CRC output width/slicing, so child-module context can materially help validate instance wiring during merge.
code_gap_notes: The generated fragments omit the final module header with explicit port directions and widths, especially DAR_dat_i versus DAT_dat_i naming consistency.
State constants and parameters are emitted inside fragments and need correct placement/order relative to uses in sequential blocks.
FSM_COMBO appears to treat any nonzero start_dat as write and does not distinguish the documented read/write/stop encodings, so transition intent needs spec context.
WRITE_DAT and READ_DAT transition comparisons use SD_BUS_W in FSM_COMBO while FSM_OUT uses full block transfer counts, creating ambiguity for final state-exit conditions.
CRC output is flattened and sliced manually; merge needs child sd_crc_16 interface context to confirm port names and 16-bit slice mapping.
Reset ownership and output register initialization must follow the FSM_OUT reset table when assembling declarations and always blocks.
selection_reason: S001 is included to satisfy the required current module interface/design block and identify the module role around DAT tri-state handling.
S002 defines the input ports, widths, and start_dat command encodings needed to build the module header and resolve control semantics.
S003 defines output ports, widths, and ownership for FIFO control, DAT outputs, busy, completion, and CRC status signals.
S004 defines internal registers and wires used throughout the generated fragments, including counters, buffers, CRC controls, and FSM registers.
S005 defines external sd_defines-based parameters and bus-width constants used in declarations, counters, and CRC comparisons.
S007 defines the sd_crc_16 child interface and required connection mapping for the generated CRC instances.
S010 defines FSM transition behavior for states present in the fragments and highlights conditions needed to reconcile next_state logic.
S013 defines the authoritative reset table and per-state output/control behavior for the large FSM_OUT fragment.
